priceSnapshot.note: The flush stopped. Since the midday snapshot at 63,988.7 the market has traded a 386.2-point box between 63,818.1 and 64,204.3 for seven hours and closed the day almost exactly where midday left it, 2.7 points lower. That is the single most important fact in this report and it is the reason the bias softens rather than deepens: the 63,750 reduce line published at midday did NOT fire, the session low of 63,818.1 stopped 48.2 points above the 4H EMA200 at 63,769.94 without touching it, and the lowest settled hourly close of the whole stretch was 63,892.9. The 4H EMA200 has now survived two separate tests in one day. What has NOT improved is positioning. Open interest fell another 0.58% to $2,040,525,808 and the long/short account ratio climbed AGAIN, from 1.45 at midday to 1.62 now - the third consecutive session of accounts adding long exposure into a market that is going down. And the one macro check the midday report singled out as decisive came back negative: Monday's US spot bitcoin ETF tape printed a net OUTFLOW of $91.0m, breaking a five-session inflow streak. Price stabilised; the mechanism underneath it weakened.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $63,750. UNCHANGED from midday, and it deserves to be unchanged because it was tested and held. It sits 18.7 points beneath the 4H EMA200 at 63,769.94, which after today is the most-defended number on the board: price probed 63,832.3 at 17:00Z and 63,818.1 at 18:30Z and stopped 62.4 and 48.2 points above it respectively, twice, without a single settled close beneath 63,892.9. A settled hourly close under 63,750 means that moving average finally failed on a close rather than a wick, which removes the last structural floor between here and the 63,000 handle. Because the next report is roughly six hours away, this line is now a RESTING STOP instruction rather than something a person will be awake to watch.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE back above $64,650, WITH open interest holding or rising across the same bar. Unchanged from midday. The price half is the retest-from-below of the level that broke this morning, and it is simultaneously the daily EMA50 at 64,655.33, the 1H EMA50 at 64,695.48 and a $970,508 realized long-liquidation shelf - three independent reasons the same number matters. The open-interest half has now scored on seven consecutive tests, most recently this morning when it blocked a buy at 65,368.0 that would be 1,382 points underwater right now. A reclaim on FALLING open interest is short-covering and fades; a reclaim on rising open interest is real money coming back.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from REDUCE back to HOLD, and no new trade is placed. The midday REDUCE was a trigger firing and it was executed - 25% of the spot core sold at 63,988.7. That trigger has now run its course: the level it was defending against, 63,750, was tested twice and held, and price is 236.1 points above it. Selling more here would be selling the low of a box that has held for seven hours, into the biggest long-liquidation shelf on the board. Buying here would be worse. The wallet is deliberately sitting on 55.53 USDT of cash that was raised at midday for one specific purpose - to buy the 63,800s - and price is 136 points ABOVE the $1,628,074 magnet at 63,850 with the thinnest liquidity window of the day directly ahead. Deploying that cash tonight, 136 points above the level it was raised to buy, would waste the only good thing the midday reduce accomplished. So the change is a real decision to stand still with a resting stop, not a shrug. What is genuinely new since midday: the ETF streak BROKE with a $91.0m net outflow, the long/short ratio went 1.45 to 1.62, open interest fell another 0.58%, and against all of that the 15m chart printed a clean bullish RSI divergence and 1H RSI recovered from 24.96 to 33.05. Deteriorating positioning against improving momentum is exactly what a range looks like from the inside, which is why range probability rises from 38% to 41% while bearish only eases from 44% to 39%.

overnightRisk: Five named things can move this before the ~02:00 COT report, and they are ranked by how much damage each can do. FIRST, the ETF print. Monday's US spot bitcoin ETF tape shows a net OUTFLOW of $91.0m (FBTC -$40.3m, GBTC -$52.0m, BITB -$28.4m, EZBC -$7.4m, BTC +$37.1m), which ends a five-session inflow run. The caveat is real and cuts both ways: IBIT, by far the largest fund and a +$86.7m to +$196.8m contributor on every day of the streak, is still marked '-' on Farside and has not reported. If IBIT lands positive the day flips to a net inflow and the structural bid survives; if it lands flat or negative, the mechanism that has produced higher lows since 05 August is gone and Asia will trade the second interpretation. SECOND, Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. Brent is $87.88 and has held the 4.5% spike it made during the US session, with the White House now demanding compensation from Iran. That is a live 24-hour headline tape, and crypto is the only market open to price it while US equities are shut - which is precisely the asymmetry that produced today's move, when BTC fell 1.43% against QQQ -0.30% and VOO -0.01%. THIRD, positioning. The long/short account ratio has risen through 1.23, 1.45 and now 1.62 across three consecutive sessions while price fell 1,279 points, and open interest fell 0.58% over the same stretch. Accounts are getting longer into a deleveraging. That is fuel, not support. FOURTH, the magnet. $1,628,074 of long liquidations already cleared at 63,850 and another $1,220,220 at 63,800; those stops have been restocked from above and they sit 136 and 186 points below spot, directly on top of the 4H EMA200 at 63,769.94. Overnight books are thin enough that 136 points is one impulse. FIFTH, the Asia session is already underway and JPXN closed -0.80%, the weakest of the three index proxies. The defensive answer to all five is the same and it is already in the box: a resting stop at 63,750, which is the only protection that works while nobody is watching.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull stays DOWN but WEAKER than at midday, and the weakening is measured rather than felt. Three facts hold it down. Of the twelve largest clusters in the window, eleven are long-side and the only short-side cluster sits 1,314 points overhead at 65,300 - there is no upside fuel within reach. Open interest fell another 0.58% to $2,040,525,618, so the deleveraging that started this morning has not finished. And the long/short account ratio ROSE again, 1.45 to 1.62, meaning accounts added long exposure across a session in which price went nowhere - the 63,850 shelf is being restocked from above as fast as it empties. Against that, one fact has genuinely improved: the liquidation FLOW has collapsed. In the six hours before the midday snapshot the market force-closed $10,377,727 of longs; in the seven hours since, it closed $1,134,318 against $8,925 of shorts. That is a 92% drop in the rate of forced selling. A market that is still crowded long but is no longer being liquidated is a market that has stopped falling without having repaired anything - which is a range, not a bottom, and it is why the magnet is a target rather than a certainty.

etfFlows.note: THE STREAK BROKE. Monday 10 August printed a NET OUTFLOW of $91.0m on Farside's tape, ending five consecutive sessions of net inflows (03 Aug +$170.1m, 04 Aug +$211.5m, 05 Aug +$244.4m, 06 Aug +$137.6m, 07 Aug +$101.7m). The components are FBTC -$40.3m, GBTC -$52.0m, BITB -$28.4m, EZBC -$7.4m, and Grayscale's mini BTC +$37.1m. The midday report named this as the single most important thing to check tonight, on the grounds that if Monday printed the first outflow of the streak on a day BTC fell, the higher-lows thesis that has held since 05 August loses its mechanism. It printed. One large caveat, and it is genuine rather than cope: IBIT is still marked '-' on Farside and has NOT reported. IBIT contributed between +$86.7m and +$196.8m on every single day of the streak, so a normal IBIT print would flip the day to a net inflow of roughly +$40m to +$100m. The number as it stands is therefore incomplete and directionally negative, and it is the first thing the midnight session should re-read rather than assume. streakDays is set to 0 because the streak of net inflows is broken on the data that exists now.

divergences.note: A textbook regular bullish divergence and the only genuinely constructive technical development of the session. The 16:45Z bar bottomed at 63,833.3 with 15m RSI at 18.43 - the washout low of the flush. Nearly two hours later the 18:30Z bar made a LOWER price low at 63,818.1, 15.2 points beneath the first, but RSI held 5.21 points HIGHER at 23.64. Lower low in price, higher low in momentum. It has since been confirmed by follow-through rather than left hanging: 15m RSI is now 40.2 and the 15m MACD histogram flipped positive to +13.37. This is what stopped the slide and it is the reason the endday bias eases rather than deepens. It is also a 15-minute signal, which means it is worth roughly one bounce and nothing more - it says nothing about whether the 4H EMA200 survives the overnight.

calibration.note: priorReduceFired is FALSE: the midday reduce line at 63,750 was not reached on a settled close, and it was not even reached on a wick - the session low of 63,818.1 stopped 68.1 points above it. actingHelped is FALSE but the honest magnitude is essentially zero. The midday session sold 25% of the spot core, 0.00055722 BTC, at 63,988.7; spot is now 63,986.0, so the trim is ahead by 2.7 points on that size - about $0.0015. Calling that a win would be dishonest and calling it a loss would be too, so it is recorded as not-helped with the note that it was immaterial to P&L. What the trim DID accomplish is not measurable in this field: it converted 55.53 USDT of the book into cash positioned to buy a 63,800 test, which is the entire reason tonight's decision can be a patient HOLD rather than a forced one. The judgement on the midday reduce belongs to whatever happens overnight, not to a 2.7-point mark.
